title: GRAPH contract graph-runtime/v0.2
description: Requests, results, hypothesis candidates and projection snapshots of GRAPH (Graph Runtime for Analysis, Provenance, Hypotheses). Each is a definition under $defs; graph_runtime.json_schema(name) gives a schema for one of them.

biconnectivity_answer.description: biconnectivity: articulation points (with the number of pieces their removal leaves of their component), bridges, and on request blocks (each with its nodes and edges); components: the connected components searched, null when interrupted. The dfs certificate is the depth-first forest: each node's preorder number and the edge to its parent.

bottleneck_answer.description: value: the witness's weakest hop weight (max_min) or its highest (min_max), null for a path with no hop. bound (interrupted only): no path to a target is strictly better. threshold: what the sources reach by hops strictly better than it holds no target.

capacity.description: A capacity: a non-negative integer or finite float.

certificate_number.description: An integer in integer-cost mode; p or p/q in lowest terms in rational mode.

components_answer.description: components: the listed components by first node, each with its nodes, size and the edges in scope between them (strong: whether a walk inside returns to its start, whether no hop enters it, whether none leaves it); total: the components of the selection, null when interrupted. The partition certificate lists every component the search finished (strong: in topological order), each with a spanning tree out of its first node (strong: and one into it).

critical_answer.description: critical_path: whether the scheduled graph is acyclic; if not, a cycle (with sources, the hops that reach it); if so, the makespan (cost), a critical path, with answer schedule every node's earliest and latest time and slack, and on request the topological order with earliest times. An interrupted answer claims nothing.

derivation_answer.description: derived: each derived target with its best value; underived (complete only): targets with no derivation; bound (interrupted only): no unsettled target has a better derivation (null: nothing known); derivation: every node the derived targets' derivations use, given (a ground), all (every input) or one (one input), with its value and the hops it uses. A value is a number, exact as value_exact in rational mode; for min_max and max_min, null is a given node's (no hop). The values certificate: values no derivation beats, the bound for every node it leaves unlisted (null: no derivation at all).

dominators_answer.description: dominators: how many nodes the sources reach; without targets, each reached node and its immediate dominator (null when no single node dominates it); with targets, each target's dominators from the sources toward it. The low_high certificate lists every reached node with its immediate dominator in a low-high order of the dominator tree. An interrupted answer claims nothing (every field null).

exact.description: An exact non-negative rational, p or p/q in lowest terms.

flow_answer.description: max_flow: the value (with value_exact as p/q when a capacity is a float), whether it is proven optimal, an upper bound, the net flow on each edge that carries any, and, when complete, a minimum cut: the hops from its source side to the rest and the nodes whose own capacity it cuts, adding up to the value. The cut certificate is the cut's source side.

hypothesis_candidate.description: A hypothesis candidate record. What JSON Schema cannot check (the digests, a generated id, unique test and assessment ids, a revision history) graph_runtime.validate_candidate and verify_revisions check. Calendar validity, chronology, distinct observations and plain JSON extension keys are also checked by the runtime.

id.description: An original ID, relation or type, as the consumer gave it.

incidence_answer.description: incidence: the matrix's dimensions, its exact rank, and the requested kernels as canonical bases (the reduced row echelon basis, each vector a primitive integer vector by node ID). The rank certificate names a nonsingular minor and, when the answer lists no kernel, carries the smaller one (its side and vectors). An interrupted answer claims nothing.

matching_answer.description: matching: the pairs by left node, each with the hop that pairs them; size; how many left nodes there are; when complete, the deficiency (left nodes no maximum matching pairs) and on request König's vertex cover: as many nodes as pairs, touching every candidate hop. With costs: cost (cost_exact in rational mode), and a certificate that adds the residual network's potentials (source and sink included).

pagerank_answer.description: personalized_pagerank: the top nodes by lower bound, each with an interval proven to hold its personalized PageRank (exact in _exact, nearest floats beside); certified_top: how many leading entries are proven the top ones; residual: the probability mass the push left unplaced; the estimates certificate lets a checker recompute every residual exactly.

path_certificate.description: Every product state (node, automaton state) the sources reach with fewer than bound hops (all of them when bound is null), by state then node, each with its fewest hops: from a listed state with fewer than bound - 1 hops, every move leads to a listed state at most one hop further, and no listed state ends a match at a target. So no matching walk to a target is shorter than bound (exists at all, when null), and reached lengths are least.

path_expression.description: A regular path expression in normal form (graph_runtime.paths): a step matches one hop in its scope landing on a node of its node types (any when null); seq and alt hold at least two items (alt de-duplicated and sorted by canonical JSON); repeat matches its item min to max times (max null: no bound; never min 1 and max 1).

path_hop.description: A hop of a regular path witness; state: the automaton state it moves to (the step it matched).

pattern_answer.description: exists and total are null only when the search was interrupted before it knew them (a pattern with a cycle counts its rows by listing them, so an interruption may leave its total unknown though rows exist); total counts every row even when an output limit lists fewer.

oneOf.description: A step that closes a cycle: a hop in its scope from the node bound to from to the node bound to to; it binds no variable.

type_parents.description: A hierarchy: each name's parents (acyclic); names without parents are left out.

relation_parents.description: A hierarchy: each name's parents (acyclic); names without parents are left out.

periodic_projection.description: A periodic projection snapshot (PeriodicProjection.to_dict): a cell's records, each edge with its image shift; its identity is recomputed from the records on reading.

periodicity_answer.description: periodicity: for each component of the requested images (in the infinite graph), the cell's nodes it meets, each with the image a spanning tree reaches and the hop it follows; the cycles that edges outside the tree close and their net shifts; the translation lattice they generate, as its Hermite normal form (basis) and rank (0 finite, 1 a chain, 2 a layer, 3 a framework); copies, the lattice's index in the integer vectors of its span (how many translated copies of the component run through the same space: a framework's degree of interpenetration); and each basis row written as a combination of the cycles (witnesses).

type_parents.description: A hierarchy: each name's parents (acyclic); names without parents are left out.

relation_parents.description: A hierarchy: each name's parents (acyclic); names without parents are left out.

projection.description: A projection snapshot (Projection.to_dict); its identity is recomputed from the records on reading.

via.description: null at depth 0, else the hop that first reached the node (the allOf below says which)

regular_reached_answer.description: answer reached: every node (among the targets) a matching walk from a source ends at, with its fewest hops and the accepting state that gives them; tree: the product states on their witnesses, by node then state, each with the hop it was first reached by.

regular_witness_answer.description: answer witness: one matching walk with the fewest hops from a source to a target.

request.description: A normalized request, as graph_runtime.normalize_request writes it and a result echoes it. An input request may leave out contract, mode, limits (or any limit), max_depth and a typed path's targets, which normalization fills.

injective.description: Distinct variables bind distinct nodes and distinct steps link distinct edges (subgraph monomorphism); no optional step. Default false.

oneOf.description: derivation: costs are non-negative for min_sum (as a shortest path's), any finite number otherwise; null: every hop costs 1.
periodicity (periodic projections only): nodes are images; the scope is followed both ways.
personalized_pagerank: alpha (the probability of stopping at each step) and tolerance (the residual to reach) are exact fractions strictly between 0 and 1.

components: connectivity weak (hops in scope followed either way) or strong (a walk each way); nodes: only the components holding these (null: every component); min_size: the fewest nodes a listed component has.
biconnectivity: every edge in scope (in either direction) is a link between its ends; nodes: only the components holding these (null: all); blocks: list the blocks too.
max_flow: sources and targets are disjoint; capacities as costs (null: every edge 1); node_capacity: what each node other than the sources and targets passes (null: no limit).
matching: left names the nodes to pair (node_types, nodes, or both); scope leads from a left node to its candidate partners outside the left set.
dominators: the nodes every walk of hops in scope from a source to a node passes through; targets null gives the whole dominator tree, else each target's dominators.

incidence: the matrix of the coefficients of the edges in scope joining row nodes and column nodes (disjoint sets); kernels: which kernels to list (left: vectors over the rows, right: over the columns).
critical_path: a hop from u to v means u comes first; sources (null: every node) limit the schedule to what they reach; costs as a shortest path's (null: every hop 1).
d_separation: x, y and given are disjoint; a hop in scope from u to v reads as u a parent (direct cause) of v.
spanning_forest: each edge in scope a link between its ends, either way; weights any finite numbers (null: every link 1); the forest least (min) or greatest (max) in the order of (weight, edge ID).
cycle_basis: each edge in scope a link between its ends, either way; weights as costs, non-negative (null: every link 1).
k_shortest_paths: simple paths from a source to a target, in the order of (cost, hops, start node and edge IDs); costs as a shortest path's (null: every hop 1).
min_cost_flow: send value (null: as much as possible) from the sources to the targets at least cost; capacities as a maximum flow's, costs as a shortest path's.

reachability_pairs: whether each source reaches its target in scope, from a 2-hop index of the projection and the scope; a simple path for each reachable pair (witnesses), the closure of each unreachable pair's source (certificate).

datalog: a positive, range-restricted program over the inputs node(N), type(N, T) and edge(E, S, T, R); the query's facts in its least model, each with a derivation, and on request the whole model as certificate.
canonical_form: the canonical order and encoding of a node set's induced subgraph (edges in scope, with their relations), by individualization and refinement.
isomorphism: whether two node sets' induced subgraphs are isomorphic, with node and edge bijections, or a counts or refinement certificate for a negative.

flux_modes: the elementary flux modes of the stoichiometric matrix of rows (species) by columns (reactions), by exact double description; each mode proven elementary by a support-rank minor on request.

code.description: unsupported: unsupported_operation, unsupported_mode, unsupported_contract, negative_cost; failed: invalid_request, invalid_cost, non_finite_cost, unknown_node, unknown_relation, unknown_node_type, unknown_edge, missing_cost, unrepresentable_result, internal_error; stale_snapshot: projection_mismatch, bindings_changed

timing.description: Wall-clock seconds by phase; not part of result_id.

result.description: The runtime additionally checks digests, normalized request identity and binding, counts, limits, exact arithmetic, and witness structure. verify_result checks witnesses against input records; it does not prove completeness or minimality.

separation_answer.description: d_separation: whether x and y are d-separated given the given nodes; when not, an active trail (each step a hop from parent to child, travelled down or up) and, for each collider on it, a directed path down to a given node; when separated, on request the Bayes-ball certificate (the ancestor set used and the visited states). An interrupted answer claims nothing.

shortest_answer.description: cost_exact and lower_bound_exact appear when the request's costs include a float (rational mode); there, cost and lower_bound are the nearest floats, or null when the exact value is beyond the floats. lower_bound appears in an interrupted answer. negative_cycle appears when the request gives a negative cost: null, or the cycle that makes every walk from a source to a target through it ever cheaper (a walk to it, the cycle with its cost, a walk from it), in which case the answer has no cost, witness or certificate.

shortest_certificate.description: potentials: a value per node (the bound when unlisted) that no hop in scope lowers by more than its cost, 0 at every source and at least the bound at every target, so no path costs less than the bound. closure: everything the sources reach, with no target among it. feasible_potentials (when a cost is negative): a value per listed node, and dead ends, such that every hop in scope from a listed node leads to a dead end or to a listed node at most its cost above, every hop from a dead end leads to a dead end, every source is listed at 0 or below or a dead end, and no target is a dead end and every listed one is at the bound or above, so no walk from a source to a target costs less than the bound.

oneOf.description: Every node the analysis read (the failure's region and everything it rests on), in ascending ID order, with its rank in the least fixpoint before and after the failure, or null where it does not stand: a rank proves a node stands (a ground, or its rule met by supports of lower rank), and the nodes without one are unfounded (failed, or their rule fails on supports without one).

support_answer.description: lost: nodes that stood before the failure and do not now; weakened: nodes that still stand but lost a support. lost, weakened and counts are null only when the analysis was interrupted before its end; counts are exact even when an output limit lists fewer nodes. With certificate: true, a complete answer carries both fixpoints' ranks, which prove it without recomputing them.

support_entry.description: A node that lost support: how many supports it has, how many still stand, the hops to the supports that stood before and do not now, and the failed nodes it rests on through them.

time.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time; real calendar dates and chronology are checked by the runtime.

typed_certificate.description: The states (node, position) the sources reach before the pattern's last hop: closed under the pattern's hops, with no last hop to a target, so no witness exists.

weight.description: A finite weight, of any sign.

signed_cost.description: A shortest path's cost, which may be negative.

signed_exact.description: An exact rational of any sign, p, -p, p/q or -p/q in lowest terms.

signed_certificate_number.description: An integer in integer-cost mode; p, -p, p/q or -p/q in lowest terms in rational mode.

forest_answer.description: The forest's edges (ascending ID), their number, the number of trees (nodes less edges) and the total weight (weight_exact, the exact value, in rational mode). An interrupted answer: all null.

cycle_answer.description: The cycle space's dimension (links less nodes plus pieces), the cycles (each its nodes in order around it, its edges by ID, its length and exact weight), and the total weight when complete. witnesses: de Pina's, one per cycle, as edge IDs.

kpaths_answer.description: The paths in order, their number, and whether fewer than k exist (null when interrupted).

mincost_answer.description: The value sent, whether it is all that was asked (null when interrupted), its exact cost, the flow on each hop (by edge and direction), and the certificate: residual potentials, and a cut when the flow is a maximum one.

pairs_answer.description: Each pair decided, in the request's order (a prefix when interrupted), with a simple path as witness when reachable; how many pairs and how many reachable; the index's label entries and its largest pair of labels (null until built); and the certificate: the closure of each unreachable pair's source.

datalog_answer.description: The query's matching facts in the least model (ascending, up to max_results), their total and whether any exists (null when interrupted), the facts their derivations use (or, with the certificate, the whole model) in rank order, each with its rule and premises, and the model's size and rounds.

form_answer.description: The canonical order of the nodes, the encoding (colors by position and sorted edges between positions), and its identity; null when interrupted.

iso_answer.description: Whether the two graphs are isomorphic (null when interrupted); the node and edge bijections when they are; and for a negative, on request, a counts or refinement certificate.

modes_answer.description: The network's size, its elementary flux modes (primitive integer vectors by reaction, ordered by support size then by reactions and values), how many are listed and their total (null when interrupted), each mode with its support-rank minor on request.
